34:1: Interpretation of Surah Saba It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty informs us about His noble self that He is the One to whom all praise is due in this world and the next, because He is the Beneficent and Gracious to the people of this world and the next, the Owner of all that, the Ruler of all that, as He the Almighty said: “And He is God; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and His is the command, and to Him you will be returned.” For this reason, God the Almighty said here: Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning that everything is His, His servants and His property, and is under His control and dominion, as He the Almighty said: And indeed, to Us belongs the Hereafter and the first. Then He the Almighty said: And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. So He is the One who is worshipped forever, the One who is praised throughout all time. And the Almighty’s saying: He is the Wise meaning in His words, actions, law, and decree. The All-Aware from whom nothing is hidden and nothing is absent. Malik said on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He is All-Aware of His creation and All-Wise in His command. For this reason, the Almighty said: He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it meaning He knows the number of the rain that falls in the parts of the earth, the seed that is sown, and what is hidden in it, and He knows what comes out of that, its number, its nature, and its characteristics. And what comes down from the sky meaning of rain and provision, and what ascends therein, meaning of righteous deeds and other than that. And He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving meaning the Most Merciful to His servants, so He does not hasten to punish their disobedient ones. He is the Forgiving of the sins of those who repent to Him and put their trust in Him.

34:3: This is one of the three verses that have no fourth, of which God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to swear by his Almighty Lord with the phrase: Resurrection, because those who denied it from the disbelievers and stubborn ones denied it. One of them is in Surat Yunus, peace be upon him, and it is His Almighty’s saying: And they ask you, is it true? Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is the truth, and you will not cause failure.’ The second is this: And those who disbelieve say, ‘The Hour will not come to us.’ Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.’ The third is in Surat At-Taghabun, and it is His Almighty’s saying: “Those who disbelieve claim that they will not be resurrected. Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that, for God, is easy.’” So God the Almighty said: Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.’ Then He described Him with what confirms and confirms that, saying: “The Knower of the Unseen. Not an atom’s weight is hidden from Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that or larger, but that it is in a clear book.” Mujahid and Qatadah said: Nothing is hidden from Him, nothing is absent from Him, meaning all of it. It is included under His knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him. Even if the bones have decayed, scattered and been torn apart, He knows where they have gone, where they were scattered, and then He will restore them as He began them the first time, for He is All-Knowing. Then He explained His wisdom in the restoration of bodies and the establishment of the Hour, with His Most High saying: “That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds. For those is forgiveness and noble provision. And those who strive against Our verses, they will have a painful punishment.” That is, they strive to obstruct the path of God and deny His messengers. For those is a punishment of a painful punishment. That is, so that the blessed among the believers will be blessed and the wretched among the disbelievers will be punished, as God the Almighty said: “The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise are the successful.” And God the Most High said: Or shall We treat those who have believed and done righteous deeds like the corrupters in the land, or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked? And the Almighty’s saying: And those who have been given knowledge will see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth. This is another wisdom connected to the one before it, which is that when the believers in what was revealed to the Messengers witness the establishment of the Hour and the recompense of the righteous and the wicked for what they had learned from the Books of God in the world, they will see it with the eye of certainty, and they will also say on that day, Indeed, the Messengers of our Lord have brought the truth. It will also be said, This is what the Most Gracious promised, and the Messengers spoke the truth. “You have remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection.” And those who have been given knowledge will see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. The Almighty is the impregnable, the One who cannot be defeated or prevented, rather He has subdued and overcome everything, the Praiseworthy, in all of His words, deeds, laws, and decree, and He is the One to be praised in all of that, glory and exaltation.

34:7: This is a statement from God Almighty about the atheist infidels’ exclusion of the Hour of Resurrection, and their mockery of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his statement of that. And those who disbelieve say, ‘Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are dispersed in every way’ meaning your bodies are scattered throughout the earth and you go in every direction and are torn apart that you meaning after this state will be in a new creation meaning you will return alive and provided for after that. And in this statement, his matter is not free of two parts: either he deliberately fabricated against God Almighty that this was revealed to him, or he did not deliberately, but it was confused for him as it is confused for the imbecile and the insane. For this reason they said, Has he fabricated a lie against God, or is he mad? God Almighty said in response to them, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment and far astray meaning the matter is not as they claimed, nor as they went to it, rather Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the truthful, righteous, and rightly guided one, who came Indeed, they are the ignorant, stupid liars in torment meaning: the disbelief that leads them to the torment of God the Most High and the far misguidance from the truth in this world. Then God the Most High said, alerting them to His power in creating the heavens and the earth, saying: Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? meaning wherever they turn and go, the heaven overlooks them, and the earth is beneath them, as God the Most High said: “And the heaven We constructed with power, and indeed, We are expanding it. And the earth We spread out, so excellent are the spreaders.” Abd bin Hamid said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? He said: If you look to your right, or to your left, or in front of you, or behind you, you will see the heaven and the earth. And the statement of God, the Most High, If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them up or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them. That is, if We willed, We could have done that to them due to their oppression and Our power over them, but We delay that due to Our forbearance and pardon. Then He said, Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back [to God]. Muammar said, on the authority of Qatada: Turning back means repentant. Sufyan said on the authority of Qatada: The one who turns back to God Almighty, meaning that in looking at the creation of the heavens and the earth there is evidence for every intelligent and wise servant who turns to God, of God Almighty’s ability to resurrect bodies and bring about the Resurrection, because He who was able to create these heavens in their height and breadth, and these earths in their lowness, lengths and widths, is able to restore bodies and spread the decayed bones, as God Almighty said: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes. And God Almighty said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.

34:10: God Almighty tells us about the blessings He bestowed upon His servant and messenger David, peace and blessings be upon him, in terms of the clear grace He gave him, and the combination of prophethood, powerful kingship, and numerous soldiers, and the great voice He gave him and granted him, so that when he glorified God with it, the steadfast, deaf, towering mountains would glorify Him with him, and the birds, the birds flying in the morning and evening would stop for him, and respond to him in various languages. In Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the voice of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him reading at night, so he stopped and listened to his reading, then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, This man has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said, "I have never heard the sound of cymbals, strings, or a string better than the voice of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him. The meaning of the Almighty's statement, "Obey" means glorify God. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and more than one person. Abu Maysarah claimed that it means glorify God in the language of Abyssinia. This is questionable, because in the language of the word "to repeat" means to chant, so the mountains and birds were commanded to chant with him. Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Zajjaj said in his book al-Jamal in the chapter on the call: O mountains, echo with him, meaning walk with him all day long. Ta’weeb means walking all day long, and as’ad means walking all night long. This is its wording, and it is very strange. I have not seen it in anyone else’s version, even though it has some support in terms of the wording in the language. However, it is far from the meaning of the verse here. What is correct is that the meaning in the Almighty’s saying: Echo with him means return, chanting with him, as mentioned above. And God knows best. And the Almighty said: And We made iron soft for him. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatada, Al-A’mash and others said: He did not need to put it in a fire or hit it with a hammer, but rather he would twist it with his hand like threads. That is why the Almighty said: Make coats of mail, which are coats of mail. Qatada said: He was the first of creation to make them, and before that they were only plates. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ibn Sama’ah told us, Ibn Damrah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, who said: David, peace be upon him, used to raise a coat of mail every day and sell it for six thousand dirhams, two thousand for him and his family, and four thousand dirhams to feed the Children of Israel the bread of the disciples. And measure the links This is guidance from God Almighty to His Prophet David, peace be upon him, in teaching him the craft of armor. Mujahid said regarding the words of God Almighty: And measure the links Do not drive the nail so that it becomes loose in the ring, and do not make it so thick that it breaks it. Make it according to the links. Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah said: Do not make it so thick that it breaks, and do not make it so thin that it becomes loose. This is how it was narrated from Qatada and others. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The links are the iron rings. Some of them said: A chained coat of mail is called masrudah if the rings are nailed, and they cited as evidence the words of the poet: And upon them are two chains of narration, which David ruled or the making of the heavy-duty swords followed. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in his biography of David, peace be upon him, through the chain of transmission of Ishaq ibn Bishr, and there is some discussion about it, on the authority of Abu Ilyas, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, the gist of which is that David, peace be upon him, used to go out in disguise and ask the caravans about him and his conduct, and whenever he asked anyone, they would praise him well for his worship, conduct, and justice, peace be upon him. Wahb said: Until God sent an angel in the form of a man, and David, peace be upon him, met him and asked him as he used to ask others, and he said: He is the best of people for himself and his nation, except that there is a characteristic in him which, if it were not for him, he would be perfect. He said: What is it? He said: He eats and feeds his family from the money of the Muslims, meaning the public treasury. At that time, David, peace be upon him, prayed to his Lord, the Almighty, to teach him a job with his hand that would make him self-sufficient and provide for his family. God, the Almighty, softened iron for him and taught him the making of armor, so he made armor, and he was the first to make it. God Almighty said: Make long coats of mail and measure the links, meaning the studs of the rings. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said, "I have never heard the sound of cymbals, strings, or a string better than the voice of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him. He said: What is it? He said: He eats and feeds his family from the money of the Muslims, meaning the public treasury. 34:12: When God the Almighty mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon David, He followed that with what He gave his son Solomon, peace be upon them, of making the wind subservient to him, so that it would carry his carpet for a month in the morning and in the evening. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He would go out on his carpet from Damascus in the morning, and stop in Istakhr for lunch there, and he would go in the evening from Istakhr and spend the night in Kabul. The distance between Damascus and Istakhr is a full month for those who are fast, and between Istakhr and Kabul is a full month for those who are fast. God the Almighty said: {And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him} Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Malik on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said: The molten copper is molten copper. Qatadah said: It was in Yemen, so whatever people did from what God the Almighty brought forth for Solomon, peace be upon him, al-Suddi said: It was only made flow for him for three days. God the Almighty said: {And among the jinn were those who worked in his presence by permission of their Lord} meaning: And We subjected to him the jinn to work in his presence by permission of his Lord. That is, by His power and by His subjecting them by His will to whatever He wills of buildings and other things. {And whoever among them deviates from Our command} meaning, and whoever among them deviates and goes against obedience, {We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze} which is the burning fire. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a strange hadith, and he said: My father told us, Abu Salih told us, Muawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani may God be pleased with him, “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The jinn are of three types: a type with wings that fly in the air, a type that are like snakes and dogs, and a type that settle and move about.” This is a very strange hadith, and it was attributed to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He also said: My father told us, Harmalah told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Bakr bin Mudar told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Buhayr, on the authority of Ibn An’am, that he said: The jinn are of three types: a type that will receive reward and be punished, a type that flies between the sky and the earth, and a type that are like snakes and dogs. Bakr bin Mudar said: I do not know except that he said: He told me that mankind is of three types: a type that God will shade under the shade of His Throne on the Day of Resurrection, a type that is like livestock, but they are even more astray, and a type that is in the form of people in the hearts of the devils. He also said: My father told us, Ali bin Hashim bin Marzouq told us, Salamah - meaning Ibn al-Fadl - told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The jinn are the offspring of Iblis, and mankind are the offspring of Adam. Some of these are believers, and some of these are believers. They are their partners in reward and punishment. Whoever of these and those is a believer, then he is a friend of God Almighty, and whoever of these and those is a disbeliever, then he is a devil. God the Almighty says: They make for him whatever he wishes of shrines and statues. As for shrines, they are the beautiful construction, and it is the most honorable thing in a dwelling and its head. Mujahid said: Shrines are buildings less than palaces. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the mosques. Qatadah said: They are the palaces and mosques. Ibn Zayd said: They are the dwellings. As for statues, Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: The statues are pictures. Mujahid said: They were made of copper. Qatadah said: They were made of clay and glass. God the Almighty says: And basins like troughs and firmly planted cooking pots. Jubāb is the plural of jabbīyah, which is the basin from which water is collected, as Al-A’sha Maymun ibn Qays said: Go to Al-Muhallaq family, a plate of the Iraqi Sheikh’s money, and you will be surprised Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Like a well, meaning like a hole in the ground. Al-Awfi said on his authority: Like basins, and this is what Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. The pots that are firmly planted, meaning fixed in their places, do not move or shift from their places due to their size. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and others said. Ikrimah said: Its fire place is from it. And the statement of God the Almighty: Work, O family of David, in gratitude, meaning, We said to them: Work in gratitude for what He has bestowed upon you in religion and in this world. Thank you is a verbal noun without a verb, or it is an object for it. In both cases, it indicates that gratitude can be in action as it can be in word and intention, as the poet said: Three things have benefited you from me: my hands, my tongue, and my hidden conscience. Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli said: Prayer is gratitude and fasting is gratitude, and every good deed you do for God the Almighty is gratitude, and the best gratitude is praise. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and he and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, who said: Gratitude is fear of God the Almighty and righteous deeds. This is for the one who is engaged in action. The family of David, peace be upon them, were like that, standing up to thank God the Almighty in word and deed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told us, Ja’far, meaning Ibn Sulayman, told us on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, who said: David, peace be upon him, had divided the prayer among his family, children and wives, so not an hour of the night or day would pass without a person from the family of David standing and praying. This verse overwhelmed them: “Work, O family of David, in gratitude. Few of My servants are grateful.” And in the two Sahihs: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: The most beloved prayer to God the Almighty is the prayer of David. He would sleep half the night, stand for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. The most beloved fasting to God the Almighty is the fasting of David. He would fast one day and break his fast the next, and he would not flee when he encountered God.”. Abu Abdullah Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Sunayd Ibn Dawud: Yusuf Ibn Muhammad Ibn Al-Munkadir narrated from his father from Jabir may God be pleased with him who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The mother of Sulayman Ibn Dawud (peace be upon them) said to Sulayman, ‘O my son, do not sleep too much at night, for sleeping too much at night will leave a man poor on the Day of Resurrection.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a very long, strange narration from Dawud (peace be upon him) here. He also said: My father narrated to us, Imran Ibn Musa narrated to us, Abu Zayd Fayd Ibn Ishaq Al-Raqi narrated to us that Fudayl said regarding the verse: Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude, Dawud said: O Lord, how can I thank You when gratitude is a blessing from You? He said: Now you have thanked Me when You said, ‘The blessing is from Me.’ And the verse: And few of My servants are grateful is a statement of reality.

34:14: God the Almighty mentions the manner of the death of Solomon, peace be upon him, and how God concealed his death from the jinn who were subservient to him in the hard work. He remained leaning on his staff, which was his staff, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: for a long period of time, about a year. Then when the termite, a beast of the earth, ate it, it weakened and fell to the ground, and it was known that he had died a long time before that. The jinn and mankind also realized that the jinn do not know the unseen as they had imagined and made people believe. A strange hadith has been reported about this, but its authenticity is questionable. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, Musa ibn Mas`ud told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whenever the Prophet of God, Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed, he would see a tree growing in front of him. He would say to it: ‘What is your name?’ It would say such and such. He would say: ‘What are you for?’ If it was planted, it would be planted, and if it was for medicine, it would be written. While he was praying one day, he saw a tree in front of him and said to it: ‘What is your name?’ It said: ‘The carob tree.’ He said: ‘What are you for?’ It said: ‘For the destruction of this house.’ So Solomon, peace be upon him, said: ‘O God, conceal my death from the jinn so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen.’ So he carved it into a staff and leaned on it for a year while the jinn worked. Then the termites ate it, and mankind realized that if the jinn knew the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating torment for a year.” He said: Ibn `Abbas used to recite it like this. He said: So the jinn thanked God. For the land, so she would bring it water, and this is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Tahman. There is something strange and unusual about its being attributed to the Prophet, but it is more likely that it is attributed to the Companions. Ata bin Abi Muslim Al-Khurasani has some strange things and there is something strange about some of his hadith. Al-Suddi said in a hadith he mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may God be pleased with them, he said: Solomon, peace be upon him, used to seclude himself in the Holy House for a year or two years, and a month or two months, and less than that and more, and he would enter it with his food and drink, and he entered it on the time he died. And the beginning of that was that there was not a day in which he woke up except that God caused a tree to grow in the Holy House, and he would come to it and ask it, What is your name? and the tree would say, My name is such and such. If it was for planting, he would plant it, and if it grew medicine, it would say, Such and such medicine grew. He would make it like that, until a tree grew called the carob tree. He asked it, What is your name? It said, I am the carob tree. He said, And for what did it grow? She said: It was planted to destroy this mosque. Solomon, peace be upon him, said: God would not destroy it while I am alive. You are the one on whose face is my destruction and the destruction of the Holy House. So he pulled it out and planted it in his wall. Then he entered the prayer niche and stood praying leaning on his staff. He died and the devils did not know about it, and they were working for him, fearing that he would come out against them and punish them. The devils used to gather around the prayer niche, and the prayer niche had windows in front of it and behind it. The devil who wanted to remove it would say: Are you not a skin? If you enter and exit from that side, then he would enter until he exited from the other side. Then one of those devils entered and passed by. No devil looked at Solomon, peace be upon him, in the prayer niche except that he was burned. He passed by and did not hear Solomon’s voice. Then he returned and did not hear. Then he returned and fell into the house and did not burn. He saw Solomon, peace be upon him, had fallen dead. So he went out and told the people that Solomon had died. They opened the door for him and took him out. And they found that his staff, which is the stick in the Ethiopian dialect, had been eaten by termites, and they did not know how long he had been dead. So they placed the termite on the staff and it ate from it for a day and a night. Then they calculated accordingly and found that he had been dead for a year, which is according to the reading of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him. So they continued to owe him a full year after his death. Then the people became certain that the jinn had lied to them, and if they had knowledge of the unseen, they would have known of Solomon’s death and would not have remained in the torment for a year working for him. This is the saying of God Almighty: “Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell down, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.” He said: Their matter became clear to the people that they had been lying to them. Then the devils said to the termite: If you were eating food, we would have brought you the best food, and if you were drinking drink, we would have given you the best drink, but we will transfer water and mud to you. He said: So they transfer that to it wherever it was. He said: Have you not seen? To the clay that is in the interior of the wood? It is what the devils bring to her as thanks to her, and this trace - and God knows best - is only what she received from the scholars of the People of the Book, and it is a trust, and only what agrees with the truth is to be believed, and only what contradicts the truth is to be disbelieved, and the rest is neither believed nor disbelieved. Ibn Wahb and Asbagh bin Al-Faraj said on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam regarding the words of God the Most High: Nothing informed them of his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. He said: Solomon, peace be upon him, said to the Angel of Death: When you command me, inform me. So he came to him and said: O Solomon, I have commanded you; you have only a short time left. So he called the devils and they built over him a palace of glass, but it had no door. So he stood up to pray and leaned on his staff. He said: Then the Angel of Death entered upon him and took his soul while he was leaning on his staff, and he did not do that to escape from the Angel of Death. He said: And the jinn were working in front of him and looking at him, thinking that he was alive. He said: Then God the Almighty sent a creature of the earth. He said: And the creature that eats sticks is called Al-Qadih, so it entered it and ate it until it ate the inside of the stick, it weakened and became heavy for it, so it fell dead. When the jinn saw that, they dispersed and left. He said: So that is what God the Most High said: Nothing informed them of his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. Asbagh said: I was told by someone else that she ate from it for a year before it fell asleep. More than one of the predecessors mentioned something similar to this. God knows best.
34:15: Saba' was the kings of Yemen and its people, and the Tubba'a were among them, and Bilqis, the companion of Solomon, peace be upon him, was among them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi said: It is the arak and the wild tamarisk. And tamarisk Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the tamarisk. Another said: It is a tree similar to the tamarisk, and it was said that it is the samr, and God knows best. And His statement: And some of the few lote trees since the best of these trees that were replaced was the lote tree, He said: And some of the few lote trees This is what the situation of those two gardens became after the ripe fruits, beautiful views, deep shade, and flowing rivers. They were replaced with the arak, tamarisk, and lote trees with many thorns and few dates. This is because of their disbelief and their association of partners with God, their denial of the truth and their turning away from it to falsehood. For this reason, God the Almighty said: "That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?" That is, We punished them for their disbelief. 34:17: Saba' was the kings of Yemen and its people, and the Tubba'a were among them, and Bilqis, the companion of Solomon, peace be upon him, was among them. They were in bliss and happiness in their country, their living, and the abundance of their provisions, crops, and fruits. God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent messengers to them commanding them to eat from His provisions and to thank Him by unifying and worshipping Him, and they were like that as long as God Almighty willed, then they turned away from what they were commanded to do, so they were punished by sending a flood and scattering throughout the country among the hands of Saba, scattered and dispersed, as will come in detail and explained soon, God willing, and in that we trust. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Walah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: “A man asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about Saba’: Is it men, a woman, or a land? He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Rather, it is a man who gave birth to ten children, six of whom inhabited Yemen and four of whom inhabited Syria. As for the Yemenis, they are Madhhij, Kindah, Azd, Ash’ariyyun, Anmar, and Himyar. As for the Syrians, they are Lakhm, Judham, ‘Amilah, and Ghassan.” And Abd narrated it on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah. This is a good chain of transmission, but they did not include it. Al-Hafiz Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr narrated it - in the book Al-Qasd wa’l-Umam, on the knowledge of the principles of genealogies of the Arabs and the Persians - on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Alqamah ibn Walah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned something similar. A similar version has been narrated from another chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad also said, and Abd bin Hamid: Yazid bin Harun told us, Abu Janab Yahya bin Abi Haya al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Hani bin Urwah, on the authority of Farwah bin Masik, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, should I fight with my people at the front and at the back? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, fight with your people at the front and at the back. When I turned away, he called me and said: Do not fight them until you call them to Islam. I said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of Saba’? Is it a valley or a mountain or what? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, rather he is a man from the Arabs. He had ten children, six of whom were on the right side and four on the wrong side. The right side was for Azd, the Ash’ariyyun, Himyar, Kindah, Madhhij, and Anmar, who are called Bajila and Khatham, and the unlucky side was for Lakhm, Judham, ‘Amilah, and Ghassan.” This is also a good chain of transmission, even though it includes Abu Janab al-Kalbi, and they have spoken about him, but Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of al-Anqari, on the authority of Asbat bin Nasr, on the authority of Yahya bin Hani’ al-Muradi, on the authority of his uncle or his father - he was unsure - Asbat - said: Furwah bin Masik, may God be pleased with him, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned him. Another way to this hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Tawbah ibn Nimr, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya, that he told him: We were with Ubaydah ibn Abd al-Rahman in Africa, and he said one day: I do not think that there are any people in a land except that they are among its people. Ali ibn Abi Rabah said: “No, so-and-so told me that Furwah ibn Masik al-Ghutayfi may God be pleased with him came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, Saba’ is a people who had glory in the pre-Islamic era, and I fear that they will abandon Islam, so should I fight them? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I have not been commanded to do anything about them after that.” Then this verse was revealed: Indeed, there was for Saba’ in their dwelling place a sign (al-Anfal 11:11). A man said to him: O Messenger of God, what is Saba’? He mentioned a hadith similar to the one before it, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about Saba’: Was he a town, a man, or a woman? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rather, a man who had ten children, and six of them inhabited Yemen, and four in Syria, as for the Yemenis… Madhhij, Kinda, Azd Ash’ariyyun, Anmar, and Himyar, except for those who settled there. As for Ash-Sham, it is Lakhm, Judham, Ghassan, and Amla. There is something strange about it, as it was mentioned that the verse was revealed in Medina, and the entire surah is Meccan. And God Almighty knows best. Another chain of transmission Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Hakam told us, Abu Sabrah Al-Nakha’i told us, on the authority of Furwah bin Masik Al-Ghutayfi, may God be pleased with him, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’: is it a land or a woman? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is neither a land nor a woman, but rather a man who had ten children, six of whom were considered to be in the right direction and four were considered to be in the wrong direction. As for those who were considered to be in the wrong direction, they were Lakhm, Judham, Amla, and Ghassan. As for those who were considered to be in the right direction, they were Kinda, Al-Ash’ariyyun, Al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar, and Anmar. A man said: Who are Anmar? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those from whom are Khatham and Bajila.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Jami’ on the authority of Abu Kurayb and Abd bin Hamid, who said: Abu Usamah told us, and he mentioned it more simply than this, then he said: This is a good, rare hadith. The genealogists, including Muhammad bin Ishaq, said: The name of Saba’ was Abd Shams bin Yashjub bin Ya’rub bin Qahtan, and he was called Saba’ because he was the first of the Arabs to take spoils of war, and he was called Al-Ra’ish because he was the first to take spoils in a raid, so he gave them to his people, so he was called Al-Ra’ish. The Arabs call wealth feathers and feathers. They mentioned that he gave good tidings of the arrival of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his early time, and he said a poem about that: After us, there will be a great king, a prophet who will not permit what is forbidden. After him, there will be kings who will be worshipped by the people without blame. And after them there will be kings from among us, and the kingdom will be among us through division. After Qahtan, a pious and hidden prophet, the best of mankind, will rule. He is called Ahmad. I wish I could live a year after his mission. So support him and love him with my victory with every armed man and every archer When he appears, be his supporters, and whoever meets him, convey my greetings to him. Al-Hamdani mentioned this in his book Al-Iklil and they differed regarding Qahtan in three statements One of them is that he is from the lineage of Iram bin Sam bin Noah, and they differed about how his lineage is connected to him in three ways. The second is that he is from the lineage of Eber, who is Hud, peace be upon him, and they also differed about how his lineage is connected to him in three ways as well. The third is that he is from the lineage of Ishmael, son of Abraham, peace be upon them both, and they differed about how his lineage is connected in three ways as well. This was mentioned in detail by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr Al-Namri, may God have mercy on him, in his book entitled Al-Inbah ala Dhikr Usul Al-Qabail Al-Rawat. The meaning of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: He was a man from the Arabs means the pure Arabs who were before Abraham, peace be upon him, from the lineage of Sam, son of Noah. According to the third opinion, he was from the lineage of Abraham, peace be upon him. This is not the well-known opinion among them, and God knows best. However, in Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, passed by a group of Aslam who were shooting arrows, so he said: Shoot, O sons of Ishmael! Your father was an archer. So, a tribe of the Ansar became Muslim—and the Ansar were Aws and Khazraj from Ghassan, from the Arabs of Yemen, from Saba’—who settled in Yathrib when Saba’ dispersed throughout the land when God, the Almighty, sent the flood of Al-Arim upon them. A group of them settled in Ash-Sham, but it was only said that it was Yemen, and they were called Ghassan, because of a water source they settled at. It was said that it was close to Al-Mashallal, as Hassan ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: If you ask, we are a noble tribe of Azd, our lineage and water are Ghassan The meaning of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ten Arabs were born to him means that these ten were from his descendants, to whom the origins of the tribes of the Arabs of Yemen go back, not that they were born from his loins, but rather among them were those who were related to him by two or three parents, or by more or less, as is established and explained in its places in the books of genealogy. The meaning of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: And six of them were considered to be on the right and four of them were considered to be on the wrong, is that after God sent the flood of Al-Arim upon them, some of them stayed in their country, and some of them moved away from it to another. The matter of the dam was that the water came to them from between two mountains, and their rain torrents and valleys also gathered to it, so their ancient kings built a great, solid dam between them, until the water rose and controlled the edges of those two mountains. They planted trees and harvested the fruits in the most abundant and beautiful way, as more than one of the predecessors mentioned, including Qatada, that the woman used to walk under the trees, and on her head was a basket or a basket, which is what the fruits are scooped into, and what would fall from the trees would fill it without needing any effort or picking because of its abundance, ripeness and quality. This dam was in Ma’rib. A town three stages from Sana'a, known as the Marib Dam. Others have mentioned that there were no flies, mosquitoes, fleas, or any other pests in their town, due to the moderate air, healthy temperament, and God's care for them so that they would unify and worship Him, as He, the Blessed and Most High, said: There was certainly for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign. Then He explained it by saying, the Almighty and Majestic: Two gardens on the right and on the left, meaning on the sides of the two mountains, and the town is between them. "Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord," meaning Forgiving to you if you persist in monotheism. Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a mighty throne. I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God. And Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: God Almighty sent to them thirteen prophets. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty sent to them twelve thousand prophets, and God knows best. When fate came, the rat overcame the cats and entered the dam, gnawed at it, and it collapsed on them. 34:18: The Almighty mentions the blessings, happiness, comfortable and prosperous life they were in, the soft lands, the safe places, the connected villages close to each other with many trees, crops and fruits such that their traveler did not need to carry provisions or water, but wherever he stopped he found water and fruits and he would take a nap in one village and spend the night in another as much as they needed on their journey. For this reason the Almighty said: And We placed between them and the towns which We have blessed. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are towns in Sana’a, and Abu Malik said the same. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others: He means the towns of Ash-Sham, meaning that they were travelling from Yemen to Yemen to Ash-Sham in visible, connected villages. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The towns that We have blessed are Jerusalem. Al-Awfi also said on his authority: They are Arab towns between Madinah and Ash-Sham. Clear towns means clear and obvious, known to travelers, who rest in one and spend the night in another. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We have measured therein the journeys meaning We made them according to what travelers need. Travel therein nights and days in security meaning security is achieved for them in their travels by night and day. Then they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves. Others read lengthen between our journeys. This is because they were arrogant about this blessing, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said. They loved deserts and wildernesses, which they needed to cross with provisions and mounts and travel in heat and fear, just as the Children of Israel asked Moses to bring forth for them from what the earth grows of its vegetables, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions, even though they were living a comfortable life with manna and quails and whatever they desired of food, drink, and fine clothing. For this reason, He said to them: Would you exchange that which is better for that which is lesser? Go down to Egypt, for you will have what you asked for. And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they incurred wrath from God. And God the Almighty said: And how many a city have We destroyed which was insolent in its life. And God the Almighty said: “And God presents an example: a city which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of God. So God made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.” And God the Almighty said about these al-Nas 114:And they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves, meaning by their disbelief, So We made them stories and dispersed them completely. Meaning, We made them a topic of conversation for the people and a source of gossip to talk about their story, and how God plotted against them and scattered them after they had been united, united, and lived a comfortable life. They dispersed here and there in the lands. That is why the Arabs say about a people when they disperse: They dispersed like the hands of Saba’ and the hands of Saba’, and They dispersed in scattered fragments. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told us: I heard my father say: I heard Ikrimah narrating the hadith of the people of Saba’. He said: “There was certainly a sign for Sheba in their dwelling place: two gardens on the right and on the left. Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord. But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam.” There were priests among them, and the devils were eavesdropping, so they informed the priests of some report from heaven. There was a noble, wealthy priest among them, and he was informed that the end of their affair was near and that the punishment had overtaken them. He did not know what to do because he had a lot of money in real estate. So he said to one of his sons, who was the most honorable of their maternal uncles: O my son, if tomorrow comes and I command you to do something, do not do it. If I rebuke you, rebuke me. If I slap you, slap me. He said: O my father, do not do it. This is a great matter and a severe matter. He said: O my son, something has happened that must happen. He kept on at him until he met him in that state. When… They woke up and the people gathered. He said: My son, do such and such. He refused, so his father rebuked him, and he complied. This continued between them until his father grabbed him and slapped him. He jumped on his father and slapped him. He said: My son slaps me? Bring me the knife. They said: What will you do with the knife? He said: Slaughter him. They said: Do you want to slaughter your son? He said: So they sent to his maternal uncles and informed them of that. His maternal uncles came and said: Take from us whatever you want, but he refused unless he slaughtered it. They said: You will die before you slaughter it. He said: If the conversation is like this, then I do not think that I will stay in a country where my son is prevented from me. Buy my house from me, buy my land from me. He continued until he sold his house, his land and his property. When the price was in his hand and he had secured it, he said: O people, the torment has come upon you and the end of your affair is near. So whoever among you wants a new house, severe fever and a long journey, let him go to Oman. And whoever among you wants wine, leavened bread and juice. And a word Ibrahim said that I did not remember - let him go to Busra. And whoever wants those firmly rooted in the mud - those who eat in the place and live in the shallows - let him go to Yathrib with its palm trees. So his people obeyed him, and the people of Oman went out to Oman. Ghassan went out to Busra, and the Aws, Khazraj and Banu Uthman went out to Yathrib, the city of palm trees. He said: They came to Batn Marr, and the Banu Uthman said: This is a good place, we do not seek a replacement for it, so they stayed there and were called Khuza’a for that reason, because they were defeated by their companions. The Aws and Khazraj remained steadfast until they settled in Medina, and the people of Oman headed to Oman and Ghassan headed to Busra. This is a strange and amazing trace, and this priest is Amr ibn Amir, one of the leaders of Yemen and the notables of Saba and their priests. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned at the beginning of the biography what happened to Amr ibn Amir, who was the first to leave the land of Yemen because he sensed that the dam had been sent against them. He said: The reason for Amr ibn Amir leaving Yemen, as Abu Zaid al-Ansari told me, was that he saw a rat digging in the Ma’rib Dam, which was holding back water from them, so they could divert it wherever they wanted in their land. He knew that the dam would not remain like that, so he decided to move from Yemen, as was the case with his people. He ordered his youngest son, if he was rude to him and slapped him, to go up to him and slap him. So his son did what he ordered him to do, and Amr said: I will not stay in a country where my youngest son slapped me in the face and exposed his wealth. Then some of the nobles of Yemen took advantage of Amr’s anger and bought his wealth, while he moved with his children and grandchildren. The Azd tribe said: We will not stay behind Amr ibn Amir. So they sold their wealth and went out with him. They set out until they reached the land of ‘Ak, passing through and visiting different countries. ‘Ak fought them, and their war was fierce. Abbas ibn Murdas al-Sulami, may God be pleased with him, said about that: And Uqayq ibn Adnan who played with Ghassan until they expelled everyone This verse is from a poem of his. He said: Then they departed from them and dispersed to the countries. The family of Jafna bin Amr bin Amir settled in Ash-Sham, the Aws and Khazraj settled in Yathrib, Khuza’a settled in Marra, Azd al-Sarat settled in As-Sarat, and Azd’aman settled in Oman. Then God sent a flood upon the dam and it collapsed, and about that God the Almighty revealed these verses. Al-Suddi mentioned the story of Amr bin Amir in a similar manner to what Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned, except that he said: So he ordered his nephew to take his son’s place - until he said, so he sold his property and left with his family and they dispersed. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: They claim that Amr ibn Amir, the paternal uncle of the people, was a soothsayer. He saw in his soothsaying that his people would be torn apart and their journeys would be spread out. So he said to them: I know that you will be torn apart, so whoever among you has a long-term concern, a heavy load, and new provisions, let him join a cup or a basket. He said: So that was Wadi’ah ibn Amr. And whoever among you is concerned with cities and affairs, let him go to the land of Shan, which was Awf bin Amr, and they are the ones who are called Barq. And whoever among you wants a temporary life and a safe sanctuary, let him go to Arzin, which was Khuza’a. And whoever among you wants the land firmly planted in the mud and the fertile soil, let him go to Yathrib with its palm trees, which was Aws and Khazraj, and they are these two tribes of the Ansar. And whoever among you wants wine and yeast and gold and silk, and kingship and leadership, let him go to Kufa and Busra, which was Ghassan, the sons of Jafna, the kings of the Levant, and whoever of them was in Iraq. Ibn Ishaq said: I heard some of the people of knowledge say that this statement was said by the wife of Amr ibn Amir, and she was a fortune teller and she saw that in her fortune telling, so God knows best which one it was. Saeed said, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: As for Ghassan, they went to Ash-Sham, and as for the Ansar, they went to Yathrib, and as for Khuza’ah, they went to Tihamah, and as for Azd, they went to Oman, and God tore them apart. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ubaidah told me that Al-A’sha, the blind man of Banu Qays ibn Tha’labah, whose name was Maymun ibn Qays, said: And in that there is an example for the follower, and Ma'rib is overtaken by the dam. Marble built for them by donkeys. If their water comes, it will not be thrown away. So he watered the crops and grapes according to the abundance of their water when it was distributed. They became hands that could not provide a drink for a weaned child. God the Almighty says: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. Meaning, in this punishment, torment, and change of blessing and well-being that befell them is a punishment for the disbelief and sins they committed, a lesson and an indication for every servant who is patient in the face of calamities and grateful for blessings. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman and Abdur-Razzaq Al-Ma’ni told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aizar ibn Harith, on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’d, on the authority of his father, who is Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I am amazed at God’s decree for the believer: If good befalls him, he praises his Lord and is grateful, and if a calamity befalls him, he praises his Lord and is patient. The believer is rewarded for everything, even the morsel that he lifts to his wife’s mouth.” An-Nasa'i narrated it in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah from the hadith of Abu Ishaq Al-Subai'i, and it is an authentic hadith from the narration of Umar ibn Sa'd from his father, but it has a corroborating report in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him: "It is amazing about the believer that nothing God decrees for him except that it is good for him. If something good happens to him, he is thankful and that is good for him, and if something bad happens to him, he is patient and that is good for him. And this is not the case for anyone but the believer." 'Abd said: Yunus told us from Shaiban from Qatadah: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. He said: Mutraf used to say: What an excellent and grateful servant is the one who is grateful when given something, and patient when afflicted.
34:19: The Almighty mentions the blessings, happiness, comfortable and prosperous life they were in, the soft lands, the safe places, the connected villages close to each other with many trees, crops and fruits such that their traveler did not need to carry provisions or water, but wherever he stopped he found water and fruits and he would take a nap in one village and spend the night in another as much as they needed on their journey. For this reason the Almighty said: And We placed between them and the towns which We have blessed. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are towns in Sana’a, and Abu Malik said the same. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others: He means the towns of Ash-Sham, meaning that they were travelling from Yemen to Yemen to Ash-Sham in visible, connected villages. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The towns that We have blessed are Jerusalem. Al-Awfi also said on his authority: They are Arab towns between Madinah and Ash-Sham. Clear towns means clear and obvious, known to travelers, who rest in one and spend the night in another. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We have measured therein the journeys meaning We made them according to what travelers need. Travel therein nights and days in security meaning security is achieved for them in their travels by night and day. Then they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves. Others read lengthen between our journeys. This is because they were arrogant about this blessing, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said. They loved deserts and wildernesses, which they needed to cross with provisions and mounts and travel in heat and fear, just as the Children of Israel asked Moses to bring forth for them from what the earth grows of its vegetables, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions, even though they were living a comfortable life with manna and quails and whatever they desired of food, drink, and fine clothing. For this reason, He said to them: Would you exchange that which is better for that which is lesser? Go down to Egypt, for you will have what you asked for. And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they incurred wrath from God. And God the Almighty said: And how many a city have We destroyed which was insolent in its life. And God the Almighty said: “And God presents an example: a city which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of God. So God made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.” And God the Almighty said about these al-Nas 114:And they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves, meaning by their disbelief, So We made them stories and dispersed them completely. Meaning, We made them a topic of conversation for the people and a source of gossip to talk about their story, and how God plotted against them and scattered them after they had been united, united, and lived a comfortable life. They dispersed here and there in the lands. That is why the Arabs say about a people when they disperse: They dispersed like the hands of Saba’ and the hands of Saba’, and They dispersed in scattered fragments. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told us: I heard my father say: I heard Ikrimah narrating the hadith of the people of Saba’. He said: “There was certainly a sign for Sheba in their dwelling place: two gardens on the right and on the left. Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord. But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam.” There were priests among them, and the devils were eavesdropping, so they informed the priests of some report from heaven. There was a noble, wealthy priest among them, and he was informed that the end of their affair was near and that the punishment had overtaken them. He did not know what to do because he had a lot of money in real estate. So he said to one of his sons, who was the most honorable of their maternal uncles: O my son, if tomorrow comes and I command you to do something, do not do it. If I rebuke you, rebuke me. If I slap you, slap me. He said: O my father, do not do it. This is a great matter and a severe matter. He said: O my son, something has happened that must happen. He kept on at him until he met him in that state. When… They woke up and the people gathered. He said: My son, do such and such. He refused, so his father rebuked him, and he complied. This continued between them until his father grabbed him and slapped him. He jumped on his father and slapped him. He said: My son slaps me? Bring me the knife. They said: What will you do with the knife? He said: Slaughter him. They said: Do you want to slaughter your son? He said: So they sent to his maternal uncles and informed them of that. His maternal uncles came and said: Take from us whatever you want, but he refused unless he slaughtered it. They said: You will die before you slaughter it. He said: If the conversation is like this, then I do not think that I will stay in a country where my son is prevented from me. Buy my house from me, buy my land from me. He continued until he sold his house, his land and his property. When the price was in his hand and he had secured it, he said: O people, the torment has come upon you and the end of your affair is near. So whoever among you wants a new house, severe fever and a long journey, let him go to Oman. And whoever among you wants wine, leavened bread and juice. And a word Ibrahim said that I did not remember - let him go to Busra. And whoever wants those firmly rooted in the mud - those who eat in the place and live in the shallows - let him go to Yathrib with its palm trees. So his people obeyed him, and the people of Oman went out to Oman. Ghassan went out to Busra, and the Aws, Khazraj and Banu Uthman went out to Yathrib, the city of palm trees. He said: They came to Batn Marr, and the Banu Uthman said: This is a good place, we do not seek a replacement for it, so they stayed there and were called Khuza’a for that reason, because they were defeated by their companions. The Aws and Khazraj remained steadfast until they settled in Medina, and the people of Oman headed to Oman and Ghassan headed to Busra. This is a strange and amazing trace, and this priest is Amr ibn Amir, one of the leaders of Yemen and the notables of Saba and their priests. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned at the beginning of the biography what happened to Amr ibn Amir, who was the first to leave the land of Yemen because he sensed that the dam had been sent against them. He said: The reason for Amr ibn Amir leaving Yemen, as Abu Zaid al-Ansari told me, was that he saw a rat digging in the Ma’rib Dam, which was holding back water from them, so they could divert it wherever they wanted in their land. He knew that the dam would not remain like that, so he decided to move from Yemen, as was the case with his people. He ordered his youngest son, if he was rude to him and slapped him, to go up to him and slap him. So his son did what he ordered him to do, and Amr said: I will not stay in a country where my youngest son slapped me in the face and exposed his wealth. Then some of the nobles of Yemen took advantage of Amr’s anger and bought his wealth, while he moved with his children and grandchildren. The Azd tribe said: We will not stay behind Amr ibn Amir. So they sold their wealth and went out with him. They set out until they reached the land of ‘Ak, passing through and visiting different countries. ‘Ak fought them, and their war was fierce. Abbas ibn Murdas al-Sulami, may God be pleased with him, said about that: And Uqayq ibn Adnan who played with Ghassan until they expelled everyone This verse is from a poem of his. He said: Then they departed from them and dispersed to the countries. The family of Jafna bin Amr bin Amir settled in Ash-Sham, the Aws and Khazraj settled in Yathrib, Khuza’a settled in Marra, Azd al-Sarat settled in As-Sarat, and Azd’aman settled in Oman. Then God sent a flood upon the dam and it collapsed, and about that God the Almighty revealed these verses. Al-Suddi mentioned the story of Amr bin Amir in a similar manner to what Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned, except that he said: So he ordered his nephew to take his son’s place - until he said, so he sold his property and left with his family and they dispersed. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: They claim that Amr ibn Amir, the paternal uncle of the people, was a soothsayer. He saw in his soothsaying that his people would be torn apart and their journeys would be spread out. So he said to them: I know that you will be torn apart, so whoever among you has a long-term concern, a heavy load, and new provisions, let him join a cup or a basket. He said: So that was Wadi’ah ibn Amr. And whoever among you is concerned with cities and affairs, let him go to the land of Shan, which was Awf bin Amr, and they are the ones who are called Barq. And whoever among you wants a temporary life and a safe sanctuary, let him go to Arzin, which was Khuza’a. And whoever among you wants the land firmly planted in the mud and the fertile soil, let him go to Yathrib with its palm trees, which was Aws and Khazraj, and they are these two tribes of the Ansar. And whoever among you wants wine and yeast and gold and silk, and kingship and leadership, let him go to Kufa and Busra, which was Ghassan, the sons of Jafna, the kings of the Levant, and whoever of them was in Iraq. Ibn Ishaq said: I heard some of the people of knowledge say that this statement was said by the wife of Amr ibn Amir, and she was a fortune teller and she saw that in her fortune telling, so God knows best which one it was. Saeed said, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: As for Ghassan, they went to Ash-Sham, and as for the Ansar, they went to Yathrib, and as for Khuza’ah, they went to Tihamah, and as for Azd, they went to Oman, and God tore them apart. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Then Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ubaidah told me that Al-A’sha, the blind man of Banu Qays ibn Tha’labah, whose name was Maymun ibn Qays, said: And in that there is an example for the follower, and Ma'rib is overtaken by the dam. Marble built for them by donkeys. If their water comes, it will not be thrown away. So he watered the crops and grapes according to the abundance of their water when it was distributed. They became hands that could not provide a drink for a weaned child. God the Almighty says: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. Meaning, in this punishment, torment, and change of blessing and well-being that befell them is a punishment for the disbelief and sins they committed, a lesson and an indication for every servant who is patient in the face of calamities and grateful for blessings. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman and Abdur-Razzaq Al-Ma’ni told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aizar ibn Harith, on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’d, on the authority of his father, who is Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I am amazed at God’s decree for the believer: If good befalls him, he praises his Lord and is grateful, and if a calamity befalls him, he praises his Lord and is patient. The believer is rewarded for everything, even the morsel that he lifts to his wife’s mouth.” An-Nasa'i narrated it in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah from the hadith of Abu Ishaq Al-Subai'i, and it is an authentic hadith from the narration of Umar ibn Sa'd from his father, but it has a corroborating report in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him: "It is amazing about the believer that nothing God decrees for him except that it is good for him. If something good happens to him, he is thankful and that is good for him, and if something bad happens to him, he is patient and that is good for him. And this is not the case for anyone but the believer." 'Abd said: Yunus told us from Shaiban from Qatadah: "Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful." He said: Mutraf used to say: What an excellent and grateful servant is the one who is grateful when given something, and patient when afflicted."
34:20: When God the Almighty mentioned the story of Sheba and what happened to them in following their whims and Satan, He informed us about them and their likes who followed Satan and whims and went against guidance and righteousness, saying: And Satan has certainly fulfilled his assumption about them. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and others, said: This verse is like what God the Almighty said when he informed us about Satan when he refused to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him, then he said: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his offspring, except for a few. And He said: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful. There are many verses about this. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When God sent Adam, peace be upon him, down from Paradise with Eve, Satan came down, happy with what he had taken from them, and he said: If you have taken from the parents what you have taken, then the offspring are weaker and weaker. This was an assumption of Satan, so God the Almighty revealed And Satan proved true his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of believers. Then Satan said: “I will not leave the son of Adam as long as he has a soul. I prepare for him, give him hopes, and deceive him.” Then God the Most High said: “By My glory and majesty, I will not withhold repentance from him as long as he is not at the point of death, and he does not call upon Me except that I answer him, and he does not ask Me except that I give him, and he does not seek forgiveness except that I forgive him.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God the Almighty said: And he had no authority over them. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: That is, no argument. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: “By God, he did not hit them with a stick, nor did he force them to do anything. It was nothing but delusion and wishful thinking. He invited them to it, and they responded to him.” God the Almighty said: Except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. That is, We only gave him authority over them to make evident who believes in the Hereafter, its establishment, its accountability, and its reward, so that he would worship his Lord the Almighty in this world better than those who are in doubt about it. And the Almighty says: And your Lord is Guardian over all things. That is, despite His protection, those of Satan’s followers who went astray went astray, and due to His protection and guardianship, those of the believers who followed the Messengers were saved.
