34:22: The Blessed and Exalted made it clear that He is the One God, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient, who has no equal or partner. Rather, He is the One who is independent in the matter alone, without a partner, disputer, or opponent. He said: Say, ‘Call upon those you claim besides God.’ They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth.’ Just as the Blessed and Exalted said: And those you call upon besides Him do not possess so much as a date stone. And the Most High said: And they have no share in them. That is, they do not possess anything independently or by way of partnership. And He has no supporter among them. That is, God has no supporter among these equals who can support Him in matters. Rather, all of creation is in need of Him and is His slave. Qatada said about the words of the Almighty: And He has no supporter among them, that is, no helper who can assist Him with anything. Then God the Almighty said: And no intercession will avail with Him except for him whom He permits. That is, due to His greatness, majesty, and pride, no one dares to intercede with Him for anything except after He permits him to intercede, as He the Almighty said: Who is he that can intercede with Him except with His permission? And He the Almighty said: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after God has given permission for whom He wills and is pleased with. And He the Almighty said: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful out of fear of Him. For this reason, it is proven in the two Sahihs from more than one chain of narration on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who is the master of the children of Adam and the greatest intercessor with God the Almighty, that when he rises to the praised station to intercede for all of creation until their Lord comes to decide the judgment, he says: “So I prostrate to God the Almighty, and He will leave me as long as God wills to leave me, and He will open for me praises that I cannot count now. Then it will be said: O Muhammad, raise your head and speak and you will hear, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted.” The hadith in full. And the saying of God the Almighty: Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The truth." This also represents a lofty station of majesty, which is that when God the Almighty speaks with revelation and the inhabitants of the heavens hear His words, they tremble with awe until something like fainting overtakes them. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud may God be pleased with him, Masruq and others. "Until, when fear has departed from their hearts" means that fear has been removed from them. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah said regarding the saying of God the Almighty: "Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The truth. He says: It has left their hearts. Some of the early Muslims read it in the nominative case with the voiced ghayn, and it goes back to the first. So when this is the case, some of them ask one another, What did your Lord say? So the bearers of the Throne inform those who are next to them, then those who are next to them inform those below them, until the report reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. For this reason, God the Almighty said: They said, The truth," meaning they reported what He said without adding or subtracting. "And He is the Most High, the Grand." Others said: Rather, the meaning of the Almighty’s statement, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, refers to the polytheists at their death throes and on the Day of Resurrection, when they awaken from the heedlessness they were in in this world and their minds return to them on the Day of Resurrection, they will say: What did your Lord say? So they were told the truth and informed of it from what they were heedless of in this world. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, means that the veil will be removed from them on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, meaning what is in them of doubt and denial. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Until fear is banished from their hearts, meaning the doubts in them. He said: Satan is banished from their hearts and leaves them and their desires and that which used to lead them astray. “They said: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They said: ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’” He said: This is about the children of Adam, at death. They acknowledge it when acknowledgement will not benefit them. Ibn Jarir chose the first statement: that the pronoun refers to the angels, and this is the truth about which there is no doubt, due to the soundness of the hadiths and reports concerning it. We will mention a part of it that indicates something else. Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this noble verse in his Sahih: Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr told us: I heard Ikrimah say: I heard Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him say: The Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain on a rock. Then, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say: ‘To the One who spoke the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.’ Then a listener hears it, and the listener listens like this, one above the other” – and Sufyan described his hand, turning it over, and spreading it between his fingers – “then he hears the word and conveys it to the one below him, then the other conveys it to the one below him, until he conveys it on the tongue of a magician or a soothsayer. Perhaps a meteor catches up with him before he utters it, and perhaps he utters it before it catches up with him, and he tells a hundred lies with it, and it is said: ‘Did he not say to us on such and such a day, such and such?’ So he is repelled by that word that was heard from heaven.” Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it from this chain, not Muslim. Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and `Abd al-Razzaq told us: Mu`ammar told us, al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of `Ali ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with a group of his companions. `Abd al-Razzaq said: From the Ansar, when a star was shot and it shone. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘What did you say when something like this happened in the Age of Ignorance?’ They said: ‘We used to say that a great person was born or that a great person died.’ I said to al-Zuhri: ‘Was it shot in the Age of Ignorance?’ He said: ‘Yes, but it became more severe when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent.’ He said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is not shot for the death or life of anyone, but when our Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the people of the heaven next to them glorify Him until the glorification reaches the lowest heaven. Then the people of the heaven next to the bearers of the Throne ask the bearers of the Throne, and those next to the bearers of the Throne ask the bearers of the Throne: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They tell them, and the people of each heaven tell a heaven. “Until the report reaches this heaven and the jinn steal the hearing and they throw, so whatever they bring with it as it is the truth, but they differentiate it and add to it.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Salih ibn Kaysan, Al-Awza’i, Yunus, and Muqal ibn Ubaydullah, all four of them from Al-Zuhri from Ali ibn Al-Husayn from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, from a man from the Ansar with it. Yunus said from men from the Ansar may God be pleased with them. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Al-Zubaidi from Al-Zuhri with it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it with it from Al-Husayn ibn Harith from Al-Walid ibn Muslim from Al-Awza’i, from Al-Zuhri from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, from a man from the Ansar may God be pleased with him. And God knows best. Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf and Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar al-Ramadi told us, and the chain of transmission is from Muhammad ibn Awf. They said: Na’im ibn Hammad told us, al-Walid - he is Ibn Muslim - told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Zakariya, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God, the Blessed and Exalted, wants to reveal His command, He speaks the revelation to him. Whenever He speaks, the heavens are seized by a violent tremor - or he said, a trembling - out of fear of God Almighty. When the inhabitants of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall down in prostration to God. The first to raise his head will be Gabriel, peace be upon him, and God will speak to him from His revelation what He wanted. Gabriel, peace be upon him, will carry him to the angels. Whenever he passes by a heaven, its angels will ask him, ‘What did our Lord say, O Gabriel?’ He, peace be upon him, will say, ‘The Truth said, and He is the Most High, the Great.’ They will all say the same as Gabriel said, and he will finish.” Gabriel carried the revelation to wherever God commanded him in the heaven and the earth.” This is how Ibn Jarir and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Abaan al-Masri on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammad. Ibn Abi Hatim said: I heard my father say: This hadith is not complete on the authority of al-Walid ibn Muslim, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and on the authority of Qatadah that they interpreted this verse as meaning that God Almighty began His revelation to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the period that existed between him and Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no doubt that this is the first thing that is included in this verse.

For this reason, it is proven in the two Sahihs from more than one chain of narration on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who is the master of the children of Adam and the greatest intercessor with God the Almighty, that when he rises to the praised station to intercede for all of creation until their Lord comes to decide the judgment, he says: “So I prostrate to God the Almighty, and He will leave me as long as God wills to leave me, and He will open for me praises that I cannot count now. Then it will be said: O Muhammad, raise your head and speak and you will hear, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted.” The hadith in full. And the saying of God the Almighty: Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The truth." This also represents a lofty station of majesty, which is that when God the Almighty speaks with revelation and the inhabitants of the heavens hear His words, they tremble with awe until something like fainting overtakes them. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud may God be pleased with him, Masruq and others. "Until, when fear has departed from their hearts" means that fear has been removed from them. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah said regarding the saying of God the Almighty: "Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The truth. He says: It has left their hearts. Some of the early Muslims read it in the nominative case with the voiced ghayn, and it goes back to the first. So when this is the case, some of them ask one another, What did your Lord say? So the bearers of the Throne inform those who are next to them, then those who are next to them inform those below them, until the report reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. For this reason, God the Almighty said: They said, The truth," meaning they reported what He said without adding or subtracting. "And He is the Most High, the Grand." Others said: Rather, the meaning of the Almighty’s statement, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, refers to the polytheists at their death throes and on the Day of Resurrection, when they awaken from the heedlessness they were in in this world and their minds return to them on the Day of Resurrection, they will say: What did your Lord say? So they were told the truth and informed of it from what they were heedless of in this world. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, means that the veil will be removed from them on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said, Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, meaning what is in them of doubt and denial. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Until fear is banished from their hearts, meaning the doubts in them. He said: Satan is banished from their hearts and leaves them and their desires and that which used to lead them astray. “They said: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They said: ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’” He said: This is about the children of Adam, at death. They acknowledge it when acknowledgement will not benefit them. Ibn Jarir chose the first statement: that the pronoun refers to the angels, and this is the truth about which there is no doubt, due to the soundness of the hadiths and reports concerning it. We will mention a part of it that indicates something else. Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this noble verse in his Sahih: Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr told us: I heard Ikrimah say: I heard Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him say: The Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain on a rock. Then, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say: ‘To the One who spoke the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.’ Then a listener hears it, and the listener listens like this, one above the other” – and Sufyan described his hand, turning it over, and spreading it between his fingers – “then he hears the word and conveys it to the one below him, then the other conveys it to the one below him, until he conveys it on the tongue of a magician or a soothsayer. Perhaps a meteor catches up with him before he utters it, and perhaps he utters it before it catches up with him, and he tells a hundred lies with it, and it is said: ‘Did he not say to us on such and such a day, such and such?’ So he is repelled by that word that was heard from heaven.” Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it from this chain, not Muslim. Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and `Abd al-Razzaq told us: Mu`ammar told us, al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of `Ali ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with a group of his companions. `Abd al-Razzaq said: From the Ansar, when a star was shot and it shone. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘What did you say when something like this happened in the Age of Ignorance?’ They said: ‘We used to say that a great person was born or that a great person died.’ I said to al-Zuhri: ‘Was it shot in the Age of Ignorance?’ He said: ‘Yes, but it became more severe when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent.’ He said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is not shot for the death or life of anyone, but when our Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the people of the heaven next to them glorify Him until the glorification reaches the lowest heaven. Then the people of the heaven next to the bearers of the Throne ask the bearers of the Throne, and those next to the bearers of the Throne ask the bearers of the Throne: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They tell them, and the people of each heaven tell a heaven. “Until the report reaches this heaven and the jinn steal the hearing and they throw, so whatever they bring with it as it is the truth, but they differentiate it and add to it.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Salih ibn Kaysan, Al-Awza’i, Yunus, and Muqal ibn Ubaydullah, all four of them from Al-Zuhri from Ali ibn Al-Husayn from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, from a man from the Ansar with it. Yunus said from men from the Ansar may God be pleased with them. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Al-Zubaidi from Al-Zuhri with it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it with it from Al-Husayn ibn Harith from Al-Walid ibn Muslim from Al-Awza’i, from Al-Zuhri from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, from a man from the Ansar may God be pleased with him. And God knows best. Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf and Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar al-Ramadi told us, and the chain of transmission is from Muhammad ibn Awf. They said: Na’im ibn Hammad told us, al-Walid - he is Ibn Muslim - told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Zakariya, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God, the Blessed and Exalted, wants to reveal His command, He speaks the revelation to him. Whenever He speaks, the heavens are seized by a violent tremor - or he said, a trembling - out of fear of God Almighty. When the inhabitants of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall down in prostration to God. The first to raise his head will be Gabriel, peace be upon him, and God will speak to him from His revelation what He wanted. Gabriel, peace be upon him, will carry him to the angels. Whenever he passes by a heaven, its angels will ask him, ‘What did our Lord say, O Gabriel?’ He, peace be upon him, will say, ‘The Truth said, and He is the Most High, the Great.’ They will all say the same as Gabriel said, and he will finish.” Gabriel carried the revelation to wherever God commanded him in the heaven and the earth.” This is how Ibn Jarir and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it on the authority of Zakariya ibn Abaan al-Masri on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammad. Ibn Abi Hatim said: I heard my father say: This hadith is not complete on the authority of al-Walid ibn Muslim, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and on the authority of Qatadah that they interpreted this verse as meaning that God Almighty began His revelation to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the period that existed between him and Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no doubt that this is the first thing that is included in this verse.
34:24: God the Almighty says, affirming His uniqueness in creation and provision, and His uniqueness in divinity as well. Just as they used to admit that no one provided for them from the sky and the earth, that is, from what comes down of rain and what grows of crops, except God, so let them know that there is no god but Him. And His statement, the Most High: And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. This is an example of twisting and spreading, meaning that one of the two groups is false, and the other is correct. There is no way for you and we to be upon right guidance or in manifest error. Rather, one of us is correct, and we have established the proof of Tawhid, so this proves the invalidity of what you are upon of associating partners with God the Most High. For this reason, He said: And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Qatadah said: The companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said that to the polytheists. By God, we and they are not on the same matter. Rather, one of the two groups is guided. Ikrimah and Ziyad bin Abi Maryam said: Its meaning is that we are on the right path and you are in clear error. God the Almighty says: Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.’ This means that we disavow them, meaning you are not of us and we are not of you. Rather, we call you to God the Almighty, to His Oneness and to worshipping Him alone. If you respond, then you are of us and we are of you. If you lie, then we are innocent of you and you are innocent of us, as God the Almighty says: “But if they deny you, then say, ‘To me is my work, and to you is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.’” And God the Almighty says: “Say, ‘O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship, nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship, nor will you be worshippers of what I worship. To you is your religion, and to me is mine.’” And the Almighty said: “Say: Our Lord will gather us together” meaning on the Day of Resurrection He will gather all creation on one plain, then He will judge between us with truth, meaning He will judge between us with justice, and He will reward every worker for his deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, and on that day you will know to whom belongs honor, victory, and eternal happiness, as the Almighty said: “And on the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will be separated. * As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, rejoicing. * As for those who disbelieved and denied Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter - those will be brought to the punishment.” For this reason the Almighty said: And He is the Opener, the Knowing, meaning the Just Judge who knows the truth of matters. And the saying of the Most High: Say, ‘Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners.’ That is, show me these gods that you have attributed to God as rivals and have made equal to Him. No! That is, He has no peer, equal, partner, or equivalent. That is why the Most High said: Rather, He is God, that is, the One, the Unique, who has no partner. The Almighty, the Wise. That is, the Possessor of might by which He has subdued all things and by which He has subdued all things. The Wise in His actions, words, laws, and decree. Blessed and Exalted is He, and He is sanctified far above what they say, and God knows best.

34:28: God Almighty says to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind. That is, to all of creation who are accountable, as God Almighty says: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all.’ “Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner.” A bringer of good tidings and a warner. That is, you give good tidings of Paradise to those who obey you and warn of Hellfire to those who disobey you. But most people do not know. As God Almighty says: And most people will not be believers, even if you desire it. “And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you from the way of God.” Muhammad ibn Ka'b said about the verse: {And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to mankind} meaning to all people. Qatada said about this verse: God the Almighty sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and the most honorable of them in the sight of God the Blessed and Exalted are the most obedient to God the Almighty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah al-Dhahrani told us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani told us, al-Hakam told us, meaning Ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, say: God the Almighty favored Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, over the people of the heavens and over the prophets. They said: O Ibn Abbas, then why did He favor him over the prophets? He, may God be pleased with him, said: God the Almighty said: {And We have not sent any messenger except with the language of his people to state clearly to them} (Al-Baqarah 2:170) and He said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: {And We have not sent you except as a mercy to mankind}, so God the Almighty sent him to the jinn and mankind. What Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said has been proven in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I have been given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I have been aided by terror a distance of one month’s journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and purification, so whichever man of my nation is called to prayer, let him pray; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, as they were not for anyone before me; I have been given intercession; a prophet would be sent specifically to his people, but I have been sent to all of mankind.” Also in the Sahih is that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: I have been sent to the black and the red. Mujahid said: He means the jinn and mankind. Another said: He means the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and all are correct. Then the Almighty said, informing about the disbelievers in their rejection of the Hour: And they say, ‘When will this promise come, if you should be truthful?’ This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Then the Almighty said: Say, ‘You have an appointed time on a Day from which you will not delay an hour, nor will you advance it.’ That is, you have an appointed time that is postponed, numbered, and fixed, and will not be increased or decreased. So when it comes, it will not be delayed an hour, nor brought forward, as the Almighty said: Indeed, the term of God, when it comes, will not be delayed. And the Almighty said: “And We do not delay it except for an appointed term. The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. So among them will be the wretched and the happy.”

They said: O Ibn Abbas, then why did He favor him over the prophets? He, may God be pleased with him, said: God the Almighty said: {And We have not sent any messenger except with the language of his people to state clearly to them} (Al-Baqarah 2:170) and He said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: {And We have not sent you except as a mercy to mankind}, so God the Almighty sent him to the jinn and mankind. Those who were oppressed say,” meaning the followers, to those who were arrogant, including their leaders and masters, Had it not been for you, we would have been believers. Then all of that was falsehood, lies, and oaths. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said, Rather, it is your plotting by night and day. He said, Rather, your plotting by night and day. Malik said the same from Zayd ibn Aslam, by night and day, when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and to attribute to Him equals, meaning equals and gods with Him, and you set up for us likenesses and impossible things with which to mislead us. My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, al-Tayyib Abu al-Hasan told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Khushani, who said: There is no house in Hell, no cave, no chain, no shackle, and no chain except that the name of its inhabitant is written on it. He said: So I told it to Abu Sulayman, meaning al-Darani, may God have mercy on him, and he wept and then said: Woe to you! What would it be like if all of this were combined against him, and he put the shackles and shackles on his hands and the chain around his neck, then he was put into the Fire and put into the cave? 34:34: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanding us to follow the example of the Messengers who came before him, and informing him that He did not send a prophet to a city except that its affluent denied him and their weak followed him, as the people of Noah, peace be upon him, said, Shall we believe in you while the most base have followed you? “And we do not see you followed by anyone except the most base among us at first sight.” And the notables of the people of Salih said, “To those who were deemed weak, to those among them who believed, ‘Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord?’ They said, ‘Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent.’ Those who were arrogant said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that in which you have believed.’” And God Almighty said, And thus We have tried some of them by others so that they may say, ‘Are these from among us whom God has bestowed favor?’ Is not God most knowing of the grateful? And God Almighty said, And thus We have appointed in every city its greatest criminals so that they may plot therein. And God Almighty said, And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein; so the Word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction. And God Almighty said, And here it is said: And We did not send to any city a warner meaning a prophet or messenger but its affluent said and they are the ones with luxury, prestige, wealth and leadership. Qatada said: They are their tyrants, leaders and chiefs in evil Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers meaning we do not believe in it nor do we follow it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Harun bin Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: There were two men who were partners, one of them went out to the coast and the other stayed behind. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a message, he wrote to his companion asking him what he had done. So he wrote to him that no one from Quraysh followed him, only the most lowly and needy of the people followed him. He said: So he left his business and came to his friend and said: Guide me to him. He said: He was reading books or some books. He said: So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What do you call to? He said: I call to such and such. He said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you know that? He said: No prophet was sent except that the most lowly and needy of the people followed him. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “And We did not send a warner to a city but its affluent said: Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.” He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him word that God, the Almighty, had revealed confirmation of what you had said. And this is what Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him about those matters. He said: And I asked you, will the weak among the people follow him or their nobles? You claimed, rather, the weak among them are the followers of the Messengers. God the Almighty said, informing us about the luxurious deniers: And they say, ‘We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished.’ That is, they boasted about their abundance of wealth and children, and believed that this was evidence of God’s love for them and His care for them, and that He would not give them this in this world and then punish them in the Hereafter, but that is impossible for them. God the Almighty said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive. God the Almighty said: “So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.” God the Almighty said: “Leave Me and he whom I created alone * And for whom I have given abundant wealth * And children as witnesses * And have smoothed the way for him * Then he covets that I should increase * No! He was obstinate toward Our signs * I will make him climb heavily.” God the Almighty informed us about the owner of those two gardens that he had wealth, fruits, and children, but they did not benefit him at all, but rather took all of that away in This world comes before the Hereafter. That is why God Almighty said here: Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it.’ That is, He gives money to whom He loves and to whom He does not love. He impoverishes whom He wills and enriches whom He wills. He has the perfect and comprehensive wisdom and the decisive and conclusive proof, but most people do not know. Then God the Almighty said: {And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you closer to Us in nearness} meaning, this is not evidence of Our love for you or Our concern for you. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him said: Kathir narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Yazid ibn al-A'sam narrated to us from Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: {God the Almighty does not look at your outward appearance or your wealth, but rather He looks at your hearts and your deeds}. Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Kathir ibn Hisham from Ja'far ibn Burqan with this same chain of transmission. That is why God the Almighty said: {Except for those who believe and do righteousness} meaning, faith and righteous deeds bring you closer to Us. {For those, there will be a double reward for what they did} meaning, their good deeds will be multiplied tenfold to seven hundredfold. {And they will be in the upper chambers, secure} meaning, in the lofty dwellings of Paradise, secure from all hardship, fear, harm, and from all evil that they are warned against. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra Al-Kindi told us, Al-Qasim and Ali ibn Musahhir told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there are rooms whose backs can be seen from their insides and whose insides can be seen from their backs. A Bedouin said: ‘For whom are they?’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘For those who speak pleasantly, feed the poor, fast frequently, and pray at night while people are asleep.’ ‘And those who strive against Our verses to frustrate them’ means they strive to turn people away from the path of amusement, following His messengers, and believing in His verses. ‘Those will be brought to the punishment’ means they will all be rewarded according to their deeds therein. God the Almighty said: "Say: 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him.'" That is, according to his wealth, there is wisdom in that. He expands the wealth of this one greatly, and restricts and restricts the provision of this one greatly. And He has wisdom in that that no one else can comprehend, as God the Almighty said: "See how We have favored some of them over others. And the Hereafter will be greater in degrees and greater in preference." That is, just as they differ in this world, one is poor and one is rich and has plenty, so too will they be in the Hereafter, one in the highest chambers, and one in the lowest depths. And the best of people in this world, as the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "He has succeeded who has submitted to Islam and has been provided with sufficiency and whom God has made content with what He has given him." Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Ibn 'Amr may God be pleased with them both. God the Almighty says: {And whatever you spend, He will replace it} meaning, whatever you spend of what He has commanded you and permitted you, He will replace it for you in this world with something else, and in the Hereafter with a reward and recompense, as it is proven in the hadith: “God the Almighty says: Spend, and I will spend on you.” And in the hadith, two angels rise every day, one of them says: O God, give to the miser destruction, and the other says: O God, give to the spender a replacement. And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Spend, Bilal, and do not fear poverty from the Lord of the Throne. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Fallas, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Kawthar ibn Hakeem, on the authority of Makhul, who said: I was informed on the authority of Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Behold, after your time there will come a time of biting. The wealthy will bite what is in their hands, fearing to spend.” Then he recited this verse: {And whatever you spend, He will replace it. And He is the Best of providers.} Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la Al-Mawsili said: Rawh bin Hatim narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Kawthar bin Hakim, on the authority of Makhul, who said: I was informed on the authority of Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "Behold, after this time of yours there will come a time of biting. The wealthy will bite back what is in their hands, beware of spending." God the Most High said: "And whatever you spend - He will replace it, and He is the Best of providers." And in the hadith: "The worst of people are those who sell to those in need. Behold, selling to those in need is forbidden. Behold, selling to those in need is forbidden. A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim. He does not wrong him or let him down. If you have something good to do, then return it to your brother; otherwise, do not add to his destruction." This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and its chain of transmission is weak. Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Abu Yunus Al-Hasan bin Yazid that Mujahid said: "None of you should interpret this verse: 'And whatever you spend - He will replace it.' If any of you has something to support him, then let him be moderate in it, for provision is decreed."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra Al-Kindi told us, Al-Qasim and Ali ibn Musahhir told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there are rooms whose backs can be seen from their insides and whose insides can be seen from their backs. And He has wisdom in that that no one else can comprehend, as God the Almighty said: "See how We have favored some of them over others. And the Hereafter will be greater in degrees and greater in preference." That is, just as they differ in this world, one is poor and one is rich and has plenty, so too will they be in the Hereafter, one in the highest chambers, and one in the lowest depths. And the best of people in this world, as the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: He has succeeded who has submitted to Islam and has been provided with sufficiency and whom God has made content with what He has given him. 34:40: God Almighty tells us that on the Day of Resurrection He will knock on the heads of the creation with the polytheists, and He will ask the angels whom the polytheists claimed to worship idols in their form in order to bring them closer to God. He will say to the angels, Was it you who commanded these people to worship you? That is, you commanded these people to worship you, as God Almighty said in Surat Al-Furqan, Was it you who led My servants astray, or did they themselves go astray from the way? And as He says to Jesus, peace be upon him, Did you tell the people to take me and my mother as gods besides God? He said, Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. And thus the angels will say, Glory be to You, that is, You are too exalted and sanctified to have a god with You. You are our protector rather than them, that is, we are Your servants and we disavow these people before You. Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning the devils, because they were the ones who made idol worship attractive to them and led them astray. Most of them are believers in them, as God Almighty said, “They invoke none besides Him except Females, and they invoke none but a rebellious devil. God has cursed him. God Almighty said, “So this Day you will not possess for one another any benefit or harm.” That is, no benefit will come to you from those whom you hoped to benefit from today, from the rivals and idols whose worship you saved for your hardships and distress. This Day they will not possess for you any benefit or harm. “And We will say to those who did wrong,” that is, the polytheists, Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny. That is, this will be said to them as a rebuke and a reprimand.

34:43: God tells us about the disbelievers that they deserve His punishment and painful torment, because when His clear verses were recited to them, they heard them fresh and soft from the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said, ‘This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.’ They mean that the religion of their fathers is the truth, and that what the Messenger brought them is, in their view, false. May the curses of God be upon them and their fathers. And they said, ‘This is nothing but a fabricated lie.’ They mean the Qur’an. And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’ God, the Most High, said, And We did not give them any books to study, nor did We send to them before you any warner. That is, God did not send down to the Arabs any book before the Qur’an, nor did He send to them any prophet before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They would have liked that and said, If a warner had come to us or a book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than others. But when God bestowed that upon them, they denied it, rejected it, and were obstinate toward it. Then God the Almighty said: And those before them denied meaning of the nations and they did not attain even a tenth of what We gave them Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: meaning of the power in this world. Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said the same, as God the Almighty said: “And We had certainly established them in that in which We have not established you, and We gave them hearing and sight and hearts. But their hearing and sight and hearts availed them not at all when they used to deny the signs of God, and that which they used to ridicule encompassed them” Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in strength meaning that this did not avert or repel the punishment of God from them, rather God destroyed them because they denied His messengers. For this reason He said: So they denied My messengers, so how was My reproach meaning how was My punishment, retaliation and victory for My messengers.

34:46: God the Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these unbelievers who claim that you are mad, I only admonish you of one thing, meaning, I only command you of one thing, which is, “That you stand before God in pairs and individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.” That is, stand up sincerely for God the Almighty, without passion or fanaticism, and ask one another: Is Muhammad mad? So advise one another. Then reflect, meaning, a man should look at himself regarding the matter of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and ask others about his situation if he is confused about it, and reflect on it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “That you stand before God in pairs and individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.” This is the meaning of what Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and others mentioned, and this is what is meant by the verse. As for the hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Sadaqah bin Khalid told us, Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “I have been given three things that were not given to anyone before me, and I do not boast about them: spoils of war were made lawful for me, but they were not lawful for those before me. Before me, they used to gather their spoils and burn them. I was sent to every red and black person, and every prophet was sent specifically to his people. The earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, so I perform tayammum with sand and pray in it whenever the time for prayer comes. God Almighty said: ‘That you stand before God in pairs and alone’. And I was aided by terror, a distance of a month’s journey before me.” This hadith has a weak chain of transmission, and the interpretation of the verse as standing in prayer in congregation and individually is far-fetched, and perhaps it was inserted into the hadith by some of the narrators, for its origin is established in the Sahihs and elsewhere, and God knows best. And the Almighty said: He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment. Al-Bukhari said then: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Muhammad ibn Khazim told us, Al-A’mash told us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Saeed ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, ascended Safa one day and said: O morning! The Quraysh gathered around him and said: What is the matter with you? He said: Tell me, if I told you that the enemy would attack you in the morning or evening, would you not believe me? They said: Yes. He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment. Abu Lahab said: Perish you! Is this why you have gathered us? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish! It was mentioned earlier when God, the Almighty, said: And warn your nearest relatives. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu`aym told us, Bashir ibn al-Muhajir told us, Abdullah ibn Buraydah told me on the authority of his father may God be pleased with him who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came out to us one day and called out three times, saying: ‘O people, do you know what my example is and your example?’ They said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘My example and your example is like that of a people who feared an enemy approaching them, so they sent a man to spy on them. While he was like that, he saw the enemy and approached to warn them. He feared that the enemy would catch up with him before he could warn his people, so he threw his garment down, ‘O people, you have been given a gift! O people, you have been given a gift!’” With this chain of transmission, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: I and the Hour have been sent together, and it almost overtook me. This was reported only by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad.
34:47: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the polytheists, Whatever reward I have asked of you is yours, meaning I do not want from you any reward or gift for conveying God Almighty’s message to you, advising you, and commanding you to worship God. The correct view is that there is no contradiction between the two opinions, because they were prevented from their desires in this world and from what they sought in the Hereafter, so they were prevented from it. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here a very strange and amazing trace, so we will mention it in full. He said: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Bishr bin Hajar al-Sami told us, Ali bin Mansour al-Anbari told us, on the authority of al-Sharqi bin Qatami, on the authority of Saad bin Tarif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire to the end of the verse. He said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was a conqueror, meaning God Almighty opened up wealth for him. Then he died and his son, who was worthless, meaning corrupt, inherited it. He used to spend God Almighty’s wealth in disobeying God Almighty. When his father’s sisters saw that, they came to the young man and rebuked and blamed him. The young man became fed up, so he sold his property to a poor person, then he traveled and came to a gushing spring, and he spent his wealth in it and built a palace. While he was sitting one day, a wind brought to him a woman who had the most beautiful face and the best scent. She said: Who are you, O servant of God? He said: I am a man from the Children of Israel. She said: So you have this palace and this wealth? He said: Yes. She said: Do you have a wife? He said: No. She said: How can you live happily without a wife? He said: That is what happened. He said: Do you have a husband? She said: No. He said: Will you not like me unless I marry you? She said: I am a woman from you at a distance of a mile, so if tomorrow comes, take provisions for a day and come to me, and if you see terror on your way, do not be alarmed by it. So the next day, he took provisions for a day and set off. He came to a palace, and knocked on its door, and a young man with the most handsome face and the best scent came out to him. He said: Who are you, O servant of God? He said: I am an Israelite. He said: What is your need? He said: The owner of the palace invited me to herself. He said: You have spoken the truth. He said: Did you see anything terror on the way? He said: Yes, and had she not told me that there would be no harm upon me, what I saw would have alarmed me. He said: What did you see? He said: I came until the path opened for me, and behold, I saw a dog with its mouth open. I was startled and jumped up, and behold, I was behind it, and behold, its puppies were barking from its belly. The young man said to him: You will not live to see this. This will happen at the end of time. A young man will sit with the elders in their assembly, and his speech will please them. He said: Then I came until the path opened for me, and behold, I saw a hundred young goats, and behold, a kid among them was sucking them. When he finished them and thought that he had not left anything behind, he opened his mouth seeking more. He said: You will not live to see this. This will happen at the end of time, when a king will gather all the silent people, until when he thought that he had not left anything behind, he will open his mouth seeking more. He said: Then I came until the path opened for me, and behold, I saw a tree, and a branch from one of its trees was fresh and I wanted to cut it, but another tree called out to me: O servant of God, take from us, until all the trees called out to me: O servant of God, take from me. He said: You will not live to see this. This will happen at the end of time, when men will decrease and women will increase, to the point that a man will propose to a woman, and ten will invite him. And the twenty to themselves. He said: Then I came until the path opened for me, and behold, I saw a man standing at a spring, scooping water for each person. When they broke away from him, he poured it into his jug, but his jug did not stick to anything. He said: You will not attain this. This will be at the end of time, the storyteller, teaching people knowledge, then he contradicts them in committing sins against God the Most High. He said: Then I came until the path opened for me, behold, I saw a goat, and behold, people had taken hold of its legs, and behold, a man had taken hold of its horns, and behold, a man had taken hold of its tail, and behold, a rider had mounted it, and behold, a man had milked it. He said: As for the goat, it is the world, and those who took hold of its legs are falling from its livelihood. As for the one who took hold of its horns, he is dealing with its narrow livelihood. As for the one who took hold of its tail, it turned away from him. As for the one who rode it, it left it. As for the one who milked it, it went away. He said: Then I came until the path opened for me, behold, I saw a man drawing water from a well. Whenever he took out his bucket, he poured it into the basin, and it flowed. The water returned to the well. He said: This is a man to whom God has rejected his good deeds, but He did not accept them. He said: Then I came until the path opened up for me, and behold, I saw a man sowing seed and harvesting it, and behold, it was good wheat. He said: This is a man to whom God has accepted his good deeds and made them pure for him. He said: Then I came forward until the way opened for me, and behold, I saw a man lying on his back. He said: O servant of God, come closer to me, take my hand and make me sit down, for by God I have not sat down since God created me. So I took his hand, and he stood up running until I could not see him. The young man said to him: This is the most distant Omar, I am the Angel of Death, and I am the woman who came to you. God the Most High commanded me to take the soul of the most distant in this place, then send him to the fire of Hell. He said: So this verse was revealed about him: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire verse. This is a strange narration, and its authenticity is questionable. The revelation of the verse about him and in his right means that all the disbelievers die and their souls are attached to the life of this world, as happened to this deluded, infatuated man. He went to seek what he wanted, and the Angel of Death suddenly came to him, and a barrier was placed between him and what he desired. God the Almighty says: {As He did with their followers before} meaning, as happened to the past nations who denied the messengers, when God’s punishment came to them, they wished that they had believed, but it was not accepted from them. {But when they saw Our punishment, they said, We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with.} So their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the way of God which has already occurred with His servants, and there the disbelievers lost out. {And they were in disquieting doubt} meaning, they were in disquieting doubt in this world, and for this reason their faith was not accepted when they witnessed the punishment. Qatadah said: Beware of doubt and suspicion, for whoever dies in doubt will be resurrected with it, and whoever dies in certainty will be resurrected with it.} [The end of the interpretation of Surah Saba’] And God the Almighty is the Grantor of success to what is correct.
